A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ImProver and contain readable main text, equations, tables, proof examples, and Appendices A–B. Retained content can be matched despite renumbering, terminology changes, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original proof-optimization experiments on MIL, Compfiles, and Mathlib, component ablations, and proof-generation results on MIL.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds mixed-objective optimization, a syntax-guidance ablation, and MiniF2F proof-generation results.

M1.justification: v2 adds an optional mixed optimization objective and corresponding prompt, penalizing each tactic by one point and rewarding declarative tactics by five. The underlying CoS, retrieval, output-formatting, and compound-sampling procedures remain unchanged; renaming readability to declarativity does not itself change the method.

E1.justification: v2 adds joint length/declarativity optimization across the three retained corpora and MiniF2F-test proof generation beyond the earlier 23-exercise MIL completion evaluation. This substantially extends the evaluated task requirements and competitive-mathematics proof-generation coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 9 adds Lean Expert Iteration as a reported MiniF2F comparator, with 34.5% accuracy. Existing GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini comparisons remain. GPT-f is discussed but has no reported comparison result; the PDF does not establish that Lean Expert Iteration was rerun under matched settings.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce mixed-objective scoring, MiniF2F pass@8 using two refinement steps with best-of-four sampling, and a syntax-guidance control on 32 MIL theorems. Existing dataset sizes and parameter-selection procedures are retained. The newly stated MIL pass@15 budget is additional disclosure, not evidence of a changed earlier budget.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted syntax-guidance/error-forwarding ablation in Table 8 and mixed-objective and MiniF2F case studies in Appendix B.3. Existing component ablations remain unchanged. The earlier MIL example compressing 28 tactics into one proof term is removed, rather than merely relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without independent repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. Newly specified pass@k budgets concern inference sampling, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Matched original quantitative results are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results under new conditions: aggregate mixed-objective improvement of 27.31 for ImProver versus 3.51 for GPT-4o, syntax-guidance ablation outcomes, and MiniF2F pass@8 of 16.39% versus 9.02%. Appendix additions and the removed single-proof-term example also change the qualitative evidence.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 introduces the mathematical definition of the mixed score: minus one per tactic plus five per declarative tactic. The original proof-optimization formulation and correctness-prioritized comparison function remain unchanged, with no new theoretical guarantee or proof about the algorithm.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow the demonstrated benefit from more readable and modular proofs to more declarative structure, consistent with the new qualifications about proxy metrics. The central claims about automated proof optimization, arbitrary user metrics, and CoS remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that its simplistic metrics need not capture human quality and can reward unused have statements. It adds interpretations of mixed-objective and syntax-guidance results and acknowledges that specialized theorem provers outperform ImProver. These substantially expand the discussion of validity and applicability beyond the earlier cost/runtime limitation.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies gpt-4o-2024-08-06, temperature 1, completion sampling budgets, and additional ablation-subset details. Appendix A adds a mixed prompt and concrete human-written prompting examples, including a stated test-exclusion safeguard. Conversely, v1's 1000-character chunks, 200-character overlap, and thread/process parallelism details disappear; the code-access information remains.

R1.justification: v2 adds prover-verifier-game framing through Anil et al. (2021), cites MiniF2F through Zheng et al. (2022), and positions ImProver against specialized theorem provers. Most related work remains unchanged; the duplicated Polu 2022a/2022b references represent an already cited work.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction, separates the metrics discussion, expands parameter-selection explanations, and condenses sampling/retrieval prose. Dataset descriptions and the main qualitative-results section move into Appendix B, while readability terminology is broadly replaced with declarativity.

P2.justification: v2 adds prompting-example figures, mixed-optimization and MiniF2F figures, and a syntax-guidance table. It expands the optimization and proof-generation tables, relocates retained main-text examples into the appendix, and removes the earlier single-proof-term example. New Table 2 also redisplays Table 1's aggregate results in transposed form.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, narrower declarativity claims, explicit discussion of metric gaming, and the syntax-guidance control improve interpretation; MiniF2F adds useful benchmark context. The net gain is limited by inconsistent new reporting, notably Table 3's positive GPT-4o mixed improvement of 3.70 alongside 0% improved accuracy, and by removal of retrieval-chunking details. The additions therefore support a limited overall improvement.
